conformance_evidence.requirement: Historical inert text and immutable Git evidence
evidence: _validate_historical_symlink_text enforces nonempty text, excludes ASCII controls and DEL, and checks UTF-8 byte length against the unchanged 10000000-byte MAX_SOURCE_BYTES.

_classify_git_blob defaults historical=False. Its historical=True and mode=120000 branch decodes immutable raw UTF-8 strictly, applies historical validation and returns text/plain metadata before magic/suffix classification. Empty, malformed, invalid-UTF-8 and oversized historical targets fail explicitly.

Only old-side builder classification passes historical=True. Old/new mode and blob IDs still come from immutable base/head tree lookups, and raw content still comes from Git blobs. No target dereference, filesystem resolution or symlink materialization is introduced.
The v1.0 relational validator and v1.1 delta validator apply the historical validator only to old mode-120000 content; all existing byte/digest and version-specific blob-OID/length checks remain.
Deletion tombstones, rename handling, mode transitions, changed-path enumeration and canonical serialization are unchanged.
New-side and full-audit head-tree classification do not pass historical=True and retain existing candidate target checks; current review-file and committed head-tree target validation are unchanged.

AST comparison against the pre-code source identifies only _validate_historical_symlink_text, _classify_git_blob, _validate_delta_entry_v1_1, validate_packet_relations and build_packet_from_git as modified/added functions. All no-follow read/write helpers, safe path checks, publication and retained artifact retrieval code remain unchanged.

Both existing packet schema versions and auto selection are unchanged. New historical text remains exact existing-schema string content, including media-looking targets and historical binary-extension names.

The frozen corpus exercises 1.0.0/1.1.0/auto with ordinary/full_audit, independent base Git identities, malformed/oversized inputs, transitions/renames, path completeness, no-follow sentinels/FIFO, consumer convergence/replay and retained/selected packet substitution.
